C. 4

To predict the number of lines in the EPR spectrum of a solution of 13C-labelled methyl radical (13CH3•), we need to consider the number of possible orientations of the unpaired electron in space.

The methyl radical has a tetrahedral geometry, with the unpaired electron in one of the p orbitals. In a tetrahedral field, the unpaired electron can orient itself in three different ways, corresponding to the three equivalent p orbitals.

Therefore, the number of lines in the EPR spectrum is equal to the number of possible orientations of the unpaired electron, which is 3.

The answer is F.
